audit_question.question: When F3 is established during recovery of an instance with prior accepted commands, can the matching prepare-reply threshold replace an already chosen value with NOOP and send that replacement for acceptance, or do supported execution configuration and initialization exclude this history?
audit_question.importance: Replacing an already chosen command sequence during recovery could allow different command sequences for one instance and inconsistent application effects. The source now establishes the replacement path and recovery entry, but a legal conflicting-decision execution has not been demonstrated.
participants: Replica whose application loop requests recovery
objects: Per-instance commands, promise ballot, value ballot and status
Configured read and write support sets
contexts: An existing accepted instance without local commit notification
Recovery bookkeeping with no client proposals
A matching prepare-reply threshold after recovery preparation
A supported configuration with intersecting distinct-participant support sets
event_paths: Prior acceptance -> delayed commit notification -> execution stalls -> recovery request is enqueued -> recover initializes missing bookkeeping and broadcasts Prepare -> PrepareReply carries retained commands and value ballot -> threshold replaces selected commands with NOOP -> bcastAccept sends the replacement
counterevidence: handlePrepare sends a full Commit instead of a PrepareReply when its local instance is COMMITTED; this can supply retained commands during recovery.
handleAccept preserves an existing COMMITTED instance and rejects lower-ballot mutation. These guards do not themselves protect replicas that accepted a value but have not learned its commitment.
handlePrepareReply rejects lower-ballot replies and routes higher-ballot replies through the nack branch; the selected replacement requires matching replies.

Fresh handlePropose admission increments crtInstance; it does not by itself establish reuse of a previously accepted instance. The immediate investigation therefore follows recovery with absent client proposals.

ReadQuorumSize returns N-F and WriteQuorumSize returns F+1. Their sum is N+1, but set intersection requires valid membership parameters and distinct participants; counters alone do not establish those premises.
F3 remains a local assignment fact. Neither prior acceptance alone nor the threshold counter establishes that a value was already chosen.
Actual delivery, ordering and supported execution activation remain unverified; source-level sends and recovery enqueue operations do not establish completed handoffs.
unknowns: Which constructor/run configuration starts executeCommands and enables the observed recovery path.
Exact Instance and LeaderBookkeeping field declarations and initial replica ballot values needed to construct a legal bounded history.
How N, F and participant identities are initialized and which concrete intersecting-support configuration is supported.
Whether a fully correlated legal history can establish prior choice, delay relevant commit notifications, and obtain matching preparation replies before a protective full Commit is processed.
Whether subsequent replacement acceptance can produce a conflicting decision under actual transport and scheduling semantics.
The client-proposal replacement variant remains outside the immediate recovery discriminator and is not explained by narrowing to NOOP.
Durable restart semantics are not established; the immediate candidate concerns retained in-memory acceptance and delayed messages.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The new source resolves several earlier gaps: handleAccept installs commands and vbal; handlePrepare reports those fields for noncommitted instances; recover preserves an existing instance and creates bookkeeping without client proposals when missing; executeCommands enqueues recovery after a stalled prefix. makeBallot only assigns lastTriedBallot and does not reset counters or adopt retained commands. The threshold subsequently replaces lb.cmds with NOOP and bcastAccept propagates it. Committed-state protections are real but local, leaving an accepted-without-commit-notification history as the decisive case. Startup activation and membership initialization are the next bounded prerequisites.

selection_rationale: Continue the same F3 establishment candidate. Source review establishes a concrete recovery path capable of reaching the NOOP branch and narrows the protection question to replicas that retain acceptance without local commitment. This is progress beyond observing an assignment overwrite, but does not establish prior choice, supported configuration, or a conflicting decision. Read the exact startup and membership initialization ranges before attributing a value-preservation obligation. The supplied inventory already distinguishes recovery enqueue and recovery entry, and outbound-consumer enrichment is already pending; no additional descriptive correction is justified here.
